Witness gold rejects and the ERC accepts: count == 10 with begin_time == null and end_time == null -- gold throws IllegalArgumentException("begin time or end time is null or empty"), while the ERC skips the whole time block and issues the GET without begin_time/end_time parameters, returning the parsed MessageListResult from a server that answers normally; count == 0 with valid times is a second such input. The other direction is empty because the ERC's only guard, count < 0 || count > 1000, is implied by gold's count <= 0 || count > 1000, so everything the ERC rejects gold rejects as well; T_erc is strictly inside T_gold.

Gold rejects start < 0 || count <= 0 || count > 500; the ERC's three separate checks weaken count <= 0 to count < 0. Witness gold rejects and the ERC accepts: start == 0, count == 0 against a server that answers normally -- gold throws IllegalArgumentException without any request, the ERC passes its guards, sends the group-list GET with count=0 and returns the parsed GroupListResult. The other direction is empty because count < 0 implies count <= 0 and the start and 500 bounds are gold's verbatim, so T_erc is strictly contained in T_gold.

The ERC restores gold's default branch with the same PluginRuntimeException, so http, https, ftp and file protocols take the same two delegations and every other protocol throws in both. Gold throws when !Files.isRegularFile(file) || Files.size(file) == 0; the ERC weakens the first test to !Files.exists(file). Witness gold rejects and the ERC accepts: file pointing at an existing directory -- gold sees a non-regular file and throws VerifyException, while the ERC finds it exists and, on a normal Linux filesystem where a directory inode reports a non-zero size (4096 on ext4), passes the size check and returns as if the plugin file had been verified. That the directory's reported size is non-zero is the filesystem-dependent part of this witness. The other direction is empty because a path that does not exist is not a regular file either, so gold throws wherever the ERC's first guard fires, and the ERC's second guard is gold's second disjunct verbatim; T_erc is strictly inside T_gold.

The ERC splits gold's single disjunction into two guards testing the same bounds, i > Short.MAX_VALUE and i < Short.MIN_VALUE; gold's casts of the constants to int are no-ops since both operands are already promoted to int. Gold's casts of Byte.MAX_VALUE and Byte.MIN_VALUE to int are no-ops in the comparison, so the ERC's i > Byte.MAX_VALUE || i < Byte.MIN_VALUE is gold's condition exactly. The same values throw IllegalStateException and all others return the same (byte) i. Only the message differs.

Primitives.java at the pinned commit sets INT_MAX_USHORT = 0xffff, which is the ERC's literal 65535, and gold's i < (int) 0 is the ERC's i < 0, so the two guards accept and reject exactly the same ints and both return (short) i otherwise. The only reservation is that gold reads the static field while the ERC inlines the value, and the field is declared public static without final; nothing in the repository assigns it, so I treat it as constant. Only the message differs.

Primitives.java at the pinned commit sets INT_MAX_UBYTE = 0xff, the ERC's literal 255, and the lower bounds are both zero, so the same ints throw IllegalStateException and the rest return the same (byte) i. As above, gold reads the static field where the ERC inlines the constant; the field is never assigned anywhere in the repository. Only the message differs.

Gold throws IOException iff offset(bs) == 0, and FsInfoSector.java at the pinned commit defines offset(bs) as bs.getFsInfoSectorNr() * bs.getBytesPerSector(); the ERC tests only bs.getFsInfoSectorNr() == 0. Witness gold rejects and the ERC accepts: a Fat32BootSector whose fsInfoSectorNr is 1 but whose bytes-per-sector field is still 0 -- getBytesPerSector() is an unvalidated get16(0x0b), so the product is 0; gold throws, while the ERC builds an FsInfoSector at device offset 0, inits it and writes it out over the boot sector. The other direction is empty because a zero sector number makes the product zero as well, so everything the ERC rejects gold rejects too. On the inputs where both throw the ERC has additionally constructed the sector and run init(), but that only fills the new object's own private ByteBuffer, which no caller can reach, so there is no separate state difference to label.

The throwing sets match: both throw exactly when len != 0 && offset + len > getLength(), gold with EOFException and the ERC with IOException, and EOFException is an IOException anyway, so the type difference is excluded and no input moves between throwing and returning. What differs is where the check sits. Both-throw witness: a writable (not read-only) FatFile of length 10, read(offset 0, dest with remaining 20) -- both end in an exception, but gold throws before touching anything while the ERC first calls updateTimeStamps(false), which stamps the file's last-access date in its directory entry, so after the failed read the caller sees a modified entry in one case and an untouched one in the other.

BootSector.java at the pinned commit defines isPowerOfTwo(n) as ((n != 0) && (n & (n - 1)) == 0), so gold rejects v == 0 and every v whose low-bit test fails, which is the ERC's condition except for negative powers of two. The only such value is Integer.MIN_VALUE, and it does not separate them: gold passes its guard and then calls set8, which throws IllegalArgumentException because (value & 0xff) != value, so that input throws in both. Every accepted v is in 0..255 and a power of two in both versions, and the same set8 write happens; the early return for an unchanged value is identical.

The ERC keeps gold's read-only guard (isReadOnly() is checkClosed() plus return this.readOnly, and checkClosed has already run, so it is the same test as gold's this.readOnly) and gold's past-the-end guard with the same devOffset + remaining > getSize() condition evaluated before any write. The one omission, if (written < 0) throw new IOException(), is vacuous: FileChannel.write never returns a negative count. So the same inputs throw and the accepted path performs the same sequence of channel writes.

Gold's `(devOffset + toRead) > getSize()` guard is not in the ERC, which rejects only `read == -1` inside the loop. Witness: `read(getSize() + 1, ByteBuffer.allocate(0))` -- `dest.remaining()` is 0, so gold evaluates `(getSize() + 1 + 0) > getSize()` and throws IOException("reading past end of device") while the ERC's `while (toRead > 0)` body never runs and it returns normally, having read nothing. `getSize()` is `raf.length()` (FileDisk.java:103-107 at the pinned commit), so the offset really is past the end. The other direction is empty: when `devOffset + toRead <= getSize()` there are at least toRead bytes left in the file from devOffset, so `fc.read` returns a positive count until dest is full and the ERC's guard cannot fire on an input gold accepts; and that guard is gold's own `read < 0`, since FileChannel.read returns -1 at end of stream and a non-negative count otherwise.

Both reject exactly the iterables that yield fewer than two elements, with NoSuchElementException. Gold detects the empty case by catching the NoSuchElementException from iterator.next() and the one-element case with !iterator.hasNext(); the ERC checks hasNext() before the first next() instead. For any iterator that obeys the Iterator contract those agree, and even for one where hasNext() and next() disagree both versions still throw NoSuchElementException on the same input. Two or more elements take the identical loop, calling consumer.accept on the same successive pairs. Only the messages differ.
